positions.name: Chime Financial, Inc. Class A
positions.catalyst: Chime announced (post-close 9/8) a definitive agreement to acquire Stride Bank, N.A. — its bank partner of 7+ years — for $590M cash at ~1.5x tangible book, funded entirely from balance-sheet cash with NO equity issuance and no additional capital contribution expected. Stride becomes Chime Bank, N.A., a wholly owned national bank subsidiary. Management guides to >$100M in net synergies from eliminated sponsor-bank fees, expanded lending products and a lower cost of funds, and says the deal is accretive to EPS immediately on closing (targeted 1H27; needs OCC and Federal Reserve sign-off). In the SAME release Chime RAISED guidance: Q3 revenue to $705M (~+30% y/y) vs. prior $680-690M and $667.6M consensus, Q3 adj. EBITDA $117-120M; FY26 revenue to $2.76-2.77B (+26-27%) from $2.73-2.75B, FY26 adj. EBITDA $481-489M. UBS and Morgan Stanley both raised price targets on the news overnight.
positions.driver: Two catalysts in one release, and they are different in kind. The guidance raise is a hard change to the printed numbers — a Q3 revenue guide 5.6% above consensus is not sentiment, it is a re-based estimate the sell side has to mark to. The acquisition is structural: owning the charter removes the single largest permanent drag and the single largest bear argument on any neobank — dependence on a sponsor bank, whose fees sit in the cost line forever and whose relationship is a standing existential risk. >$100M of net synergies against a ~$2.77B revenue base is roughly 3.6 points of margin, and it is paid for with cash on hand, so there is no dilution to offset it. SETUP QUALITY: this is a base breakout, not a vertical. CHYM gapped on 8/6 earnings and then consolidated for a full month between $31.50 and $34.44 without ever surrendering the gap; $35.75 clears the entire five-week range and prints a 52-week high ($36.18 pre-market). That gives a stop that is technically meaningful rather than arbitrary — see below. MACRO ALIGNMENT, which is the real reason this beat the rest of the board: the two forces driving the tape this week are oil and the Fed. Brent is $99 and WTI $94 after the US struck five Iranian oil tankers overnight; futures are soft (Dow -0.3%, S&P -0.2%, Nasdaq-100 -0.4%); and fed funds futures price roughly 57-65% odds of a 25bp HIKE at the 9/15-16 FOMC with August CPI landing 9/11. CHYM has zero energy input exposure and zero Middle East revenue exposure, so the oil shock does not touch it. More importantly, a Fed hike is a TAILWIND here, not a headwind: a company that just bought its own deposit-taking national charter earns more net interest income and enjoys a lower relative cost of funds when rates go up. On a day when the market's dominant fear is tightening, this is the rare catalyst name whose economics improve if that fear is realized. Every other candidate on the board was either a multiple-compression victim of the same hike (BE at 344x earnings, GLW at 71x) or a direct war bet (energy).
positions.risks: (1) ENTRY IS AT THE CHASE LIMIT. $35.75 is +10.6% over the $32.31 close, which sits at/just past this book's 8-10% pre-market chase ceiling. Taken deliberately, with this mitigation: yesterday CHYM fell 4.3% in a market-wide flush (Dow -628pts), so the gap is measured off a depressed base. Against the 9/4 close of $33.76 — the last pre-flush print — the entry is only +5.9%, comfortably inside the limit. Part of this 'gap' is a rebound, not new extension. Flagging it as a rule-edge decision rather than pretending it is not. (2) GAP-AND-FADE IS THE PRIMARY LOSS PATH, and yesterday's tape proves it is live: QCOM (Amazon AI silicon deal), IONQ (raised FY26 guide) and SEI (raised Q3/Q4 EBITDA) ALL round-tripped their catalysts inside a single session. The marginal buyer has been absent. If CHYM does the same, the stop is hit. This is exactly how the 8/28 MU trade lost $507. (3) REGULATORY RISK IS REAL BUT DEFERRED. The deal needs OCC and Federal Reserve approval and does not close until 1H27. A bank-charter acquisition by a fintech is not a rubber stamp. Over a 24h hold this is close to immaterial, but any leak of regulatory friction would hit hard. (4) CPI THURSDAY. The position is held through Wednesday's session and exits Thursday pre-market — BEFORE the 8:30am ET CPI print. Checked deliberately: the rotation window closes ahead of the release, so this trade does not carry CPI risk. It does carry Wednesday's Treasury auctions and any overnight Middle East headline. (5) INSIDER SUPPLY. CEO Britt sold 100,000 shares on 8/28 ($3.40M) after 550,000 on 8/6 ($16.46M); co-founder King sold 375,000 on 8/6. Post-lockup scheduled selling by appearance, but it is persistent overhead supply into strength. (6) VALUATION IS NOT A CUSHION. 9.1x book, negative trailing EPS, $11.96B market cap. This is priced as a growth story, so a growth scare de-rates it violently. The 5-7M share average daily volume is adequate but the name still moves 5%+ on ordinary days.
